Independent prediction models

Source: vignettes/prediction-models.Rmd
prediction-models.Rmd

PSPred(), PrinPred(), and OutPred() fit and predict in one call. They do not return or cache fitted model objects. Each result is a row-aligned numeric vector with class pd_prediction.

library(PDRobust)
data("BiSample", package = "PDRobust")
raw <- BiSample
map <- Mapping(
  baseline_time = 0,
  cutoff_time = 2,
  covariates = c("X1", "X2", "X4"),
  interest_vars = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_type = "B"
)
pd_data <- DataStandard(raw, map)
map <- attr(pd_data, "pd_mapping")

Propensity prediction 

ps <- PSPred(
  A ~ X1 + X2 + X4,
  fit_dat = pd_data,
  pred_dat = pd_data,
  mapping = map
)
head(ps)

The logistic model is fitted only on baseline observations, then used to predict every row of pred_dat.

Cumulative principal-score prediction 

p0 <- PrinPred(
  S ~ X1 + X2 + X4 + A + time,
  fit_dat = pd_data,
  pred_dat = pd_data,
  treatment = 0,
  mapping = map
)
p1 <- PrinPred(
  S ~ X1 + X2 + X4 + A + time,
  fit_dat = pd_data,
  pred_dat = pd_data,
  treatment = 1,
  mapping = map
)
head(cbind(pd_data[c("id", "time")], p0, p1))

For multiple observed times, baseline rows are excluded from the principal model’s risk set. A post-baseline row is fitted only when survival at the immediately preceding observed time equals one. Conditional predictions at baseline are set to one and accumulated within subject over the complete baseline-to-cutoff grid. For a single observed time, no at-risk indicator is constructed and all complete rows are used.

Separation, aliased nuisance coefficients, or extreme fitted probabilities may produce warnings. They do not invalidate a prediction when the fitted model still returns a complete finite vector. Missing, non-finite, or row-misaligned predictions remain errors.

Outcome prediction 

fit_data <- pd_data[pd_data$S == 1, , drop = FALSE]
mu0 <- OutPred(
  Y ~ X1 + X2 + A,
  fit_dat = fit_data,
  pred_dat = pd_data,
  a = 0,
  mapping = map
)
mu1 <- OutPred(
  Y ~ X1 + X2 + A,
  fit_dat = fit_data,
  pred_dat = pd_data,
  a = 1,
  mapping = map
)
head(cbind(mu0, mu1))

OutPred() removes fitting rows with missing outcomes, sets treatment to the requested value and survival to one in prediction data, and uses either a linear or logistic outcome model according to mapping$y_type.
